content.title: TEX Q2 Deep Dive: Margin Pressures Offset by Environmental Solutions Strength and Tariff Mitigation
content.summary: Lifting and material handling equipment company Terex (NYSE:TEX) beat Wall Street’s revenue expectations in Q2 CY2025, with sales up 7.6% year on year to $1.49 billion. The company’s full-year revenue guidance of $5.4 billion at the midpoint came in 1.2% above analysts’ estimates. Its non-GAAP profit of $1.49 per share was 6.5% above analysts’ consensus estimates.

content.title: Terex, Atkore, Wabash, Old Dominion Freight Line, and Alta Shares Skyrocket, What You Need To Know
content.summary: A number of stocks jumped in the morning session after an in-line inflation report fueled hopes for interest rate cuts and the U.S. and China agreed to extend their tariff truce. The Consumer Price Index (CPI), a key measure of inflation, came in largely as expected, holding steady at 2.7% year-over-year. This reading boosted investor optimism that the Federal Reserve will have room to lower interest rates at its next meeting, which could reduce borrowing costs for companies and consumers.
